placements.why: The deployment gate decision — requiring signed release manifests for Meridian deploys across staging and production — is an architectural guardrail. No existing strata or narrative leaf covers this; the content names an organizational category for deployment infrastructure policy.
placements.title: Deployment infrastructure as a safety surface
placements.theme: Architecture decisions encode deployment guardrails that prevent unsafe releases from reaching production environments.

placements.title: Signed manifests gate Meridian deployments
placements.theme: Meridian deployments require signed release manifests across staging and production to prevent unsigned artifacts from shipping.
placements.why: Both segments express the same deployment gate decision: src-1 gives Quinton's first-person rationale (two unsigned artifacts reached staging) and the signed-manifest requirement; src-2 structures the decision into gate, scope (staging and production), and owner. This is a thematic subject future envelopes will keep feeding — a policy that all Meridian deploys require signed manifests — not a one-time fact.
